column2: req_desc

Guest session and welcome
A first visit to `/` gets the `dc_session` cookie and lands on `/welcome`, and pressing `button "Continue"` with a typed name and `radio "Avatar 7"` selected lands on `/` with `link "<name> profile"`, keeping the same name and avatar 7 after reload and in `GET /api/me`.

Welcome by keyboard alone
Using only the keyboard, a player tabs to `textbox "Name"`, types a name, selects avatar 7 with arrow keys inside `radiogroup "Avatar"`, presses Enter, and lands on `/` with focus on the page's `h1`.

Taken name suggestions
A taken name shows `alert` `#name-error` with `That name is taken. Try one of these:` and three suggestion buttons, and choosing one by keyboard fills `textbox "Name"` so that Continue then succeeds.

Name error for screen readers
When a name is refused the alert is announced and `textbox "Name"` carries `aria-invalid="true"` and an `aria-describedby` that points at `#name-error`.

Welcome on a phone
At 375x812 with touch the avatars form a 4-column grid with every avatar radio at least 44 px square, the page never scrolls sideways, and `button "Skip"` gives a name of `Guest-` followed by 4 digits.

Name rules
`POST /api/me/name` accepts 3 to 16 letters, digits or underscores that are unique ignoring case and not blocked, and otherwise answers `422 NAME_INVALID`, `409 NAME_TAKEN` or `422 NAME_BLOCKED` with three free suggestions, as qualified in API.

Keyboard striker placement
With `#board` focused on the viewer's turn, ArrowRight ten times then Shift+ArrowLeft four times shows `Striker 8.0 mm`, `slider "Striker position"` with `aria-valuetext` `8.0 mm` and `piece-striker` with `data-x="8.0"`, and the offset never passes 200.0.

Keyboard aim and aim guide
D five times then Shift+A three times shows `Aim 4.7 degrees`, and on the opening layout `#aim-guide` reports `data-first-contact="w5"` at offset 0.0 with aim 0.0 and `cushion` at offset -200.0 with aim 0.0.

Keyboard power and reset
W ten times shows `Power 20%`, S back to 0 disables `button "Shoot"`, and Escape returns the readouts to `Aim 0.0 degrees` and `Power 0%`.

Opponent sees the live ghost striker
While one player aims, the opponent's page shows `#ghost-striker` at 40 percent opacity following the striker within 1 second, with the opponent's own aiming controls disabled and `#turn-text` reading `<name>'s turn`.

Shot ruled the same on both screens
Space shoots and `#match-root` shows `data-phase="refereeing"` until the ruling, after which both players' pages end with identical piece `data-x` and `data-y` values and both `#announcer` logs carry the same verdict line, never before the ruling arrives.

Shot submission rules
`POST /api/matches/<id>/shots` returns the stored result for a resent current `shotSeq`, refuses other shots with `NOT_YOUR_TURN`, `TURN_EXPIRED`, `STALE_SEQ`, `INVALID_INTENT` or `CLIENT_OUTDATED`, and answers `429 RATE_LIMITED` to more than 15 previews in a second, as qualified in API.

Match screen on a phone
At 375x812 with touch the whole square board with all four pockets is in view, the score rail is a strip above the board, `button "Shoot"` is at least 44 px in both directions and the page never scrolls sideways.

Touch drag moves the striker
A touch drag that starts on the striker moves it along the baseline by the dragged distance in board millimetres within 2 mm, with its `data-y` unchanged.

Fine striker slider on touch
The handle of `slider "Striker position"` is at least 48 px, and one ArrowRight on the slider moves the striker 0.5 mm.

Touch pull-back sets aim and power
A touch pull-back of half the maximum pull straight toward the shooter shows `Power 25%` within 1 point and `Aim 0.0 degrees` while held, with `#aim-guide` shown.

Pull-back cancel shoots nothing
Bringing the touch back within 8 px of the press point sets the power to 0, and releasing sends no shot: `data-shot-seq` stays the same and `button "Shoot"` is disabled.

Illegal placement shown
With `w1` at (40.0, 252.1), setting the striker slider to 10.0 sets `piece-striker` `data-legal="false"`, draws the striker in its danger ring, disables `button "Shoot"` and shows `#placement-message` `Striker overlaps a coin.`

Keyboard steps across the legal edge
From offset 0.0, Shift+ArrowRight steps keep the placement legal up to 3.5 and make it illegal at 4.0, and Shift+ArrowLeft back to 3.5 makes it legal and enables Shoot again.

Illegal placement shake
Entering an illegal spot shakes the striker's outline 4 px side to side twice within 120 ms.

Illegal placement with reduced motion and announcement
With reduced motion the outline does not move and its colour changes at once, and `Striker overlaps a coin.` is announced once in `#announcer` each time the striker enters an illegal spot.

Illegal placement on a phone
At 375x812 with touch the same message and danger ring show, and tapping the disabled `button "Shoot"` sends no shot.

Placement legality on the server
A shot whose striker centre is less than 36.15 mm from any coin or the queen answers `422 ILLEGAL_PLACEMENT`, and a distance of exactly 36.15 mm is legal.

Pass-and-play setup by keyboard
On `/play/local`, using only the keyboard, a pair selects `radio "Classic"` with arrow keys, types both names, toggles `switch "Turn the board each turn"` off and on with Space, presses Enter on `button "Start"`, and sees `<Player 1 name>'s turn` with `#board-rotator` `data-rotation="0"`.

Break misses in pass-and-play
Three low-power break shots that touch nothing (W once, then Space) show `Break missed. Attempt 2 of 3.`, then `Break missed. Attempt 3 of 3.`, then `Break missed 3 times. Turn passes.` with the second player's turn.

Board turns to the shooter
With the switch on, a turn change turns `#board-rotator` through in-between angles over about half a second until `data-rotation="180"`.

Board turn and skip with reduced motion
With reduced motion the board shows no in-between angle and crossfades in about 150 ms to the same `data-rotation`, and without reduced motion `button "Skip shot"` or K jumps moving pieces to their final positions.

Resign a pass-and-play match and save it
Menu, Resign and `dialog "Resign this match?"` work by keyboard with Tab kept inside and Escape keeping play, and confirming shows `dialog "Match over"` with `<name> wins` and `Saved to your history.`, after which the profile history shows a `Pass and play` row after reload.

Pass-and-play result replayed on the server
`POST /api/local-matches` replays the shot log with the shared model and answers `201` only when the claimed winner and scores match, `422 RESULT_MISMATCH` with nothing recorded otherwise, and the stored response for a repeated `idempotencyKey`.

Early queen returned
When the queen is pocketed and the shooter has no own coin pocketed, she returns to (0.0, 0.0) on both players' pages with `RETURNED` and `Queen returned. Pocket one of your own coins first.`, and the turn passes live on the other page.

Queen awaiting cover
With two own coins already pocketed, pocketing the queen alone shows `POCKETED`, `Queen pocketed. Cover her with your next pocket.` and `#queen-status` `Awaiting cover by <name>`, and the same player shoots again.

Queen not covered
If the next shot pockets nothing, the screen shows `RETURNED` and `Queen not covered. She returns to the centre.`, the queen goes back to the centre, the turn passes, and the opponent's `#announcer` carries that line.

Queen covered
An own coin pocketed on the cover shot, or together with the queen, shows `COVERED`, `Queen covered.` and `#queen-status` `Covered by <name>`.

Verdict word motion and reduced motion
`#verdict-word` scales in only after the ruling arrives, and with reduced motion it appears at full size at once with the same announcement.

Striker foul owes a due
A pocketed striker with no own coin pocketed and none to return shows `FOUL`, `Foul: striker pocketed. One due coin is owed.` and `Dues owed: 1`, and the turn passes.

Due paid with the next pocket
When that player later pockets an own coin, the screen shows `Due paid: one coin returns to the centre. Shoot again.`, puts the coin on its published return spot and shows `Dues owed: 0`.

Foul with own coins pocketed
When the striker and an own coin are pocketed while one own coin is already down, both coins return to the published return spots, the shooter keeps the turn, and the screen shows `Foul: striker pocketed. Your pocketed coins return with one due coin. Shoot again.`

Verdict banner timing
`#verdict` slides in when the ruling arrives and leaves after the verdict banner time, and a second verdict that arrives while the first is leaving stays visible for its full time.

Foul banner on a phone and announced
At 375x812 the verdict banner fits inside the viewport with `Dues owed: <n>` still readable, and the foul line is announced exactly in `#announcer`.

Return spots
Returned pieces go to the centre spot if it is free and otherwise to the first free point of the published spiral, the queen first and then coins in id order.

Board won with the covered queen
In a Classic match on board 3 at 10-4, when the shooter has covered the queen and pockets their last coin with 4 opponent coins left, `dialog "Board over"` opens with `<name> wins board 3` and `7 points: 4 coins left + 3 for the queen`, and the shooter's `#score-<seat>` shows 17.

Queen points stop at 22
The same last coin at a match score of 22-4 shows `4 points: 4 coins left`.

Next board by keyboard
Enter on `button "Next board"` closes the sheet and returns focus to `#board`, which then shows `Board 4 of 8`, the board loser's turn with white, the opening layout and `Break attempt 1 of 3`.

Match over at 25 points
The same board win at 24-4 scores `4 points: 4 coins left` and, with no Board over sheet, sets `#match-root` `data-phase="match-over"` and opens `dialog "Match over"` with `You won`, `Final score 28-4` and that points line in its `#board-points`, with focus inside the dialog and Tab kept inside.

Classic result in history and the wider layouts
After reload `/profile/<name>` shows a `WON` row with `Classic` and `28-4`, and the score rail sits below the board at 768x1024 and to its right at 1280x800.

Last-coin fouls and the extra board
Pocketing the opponent's last coin, or one's own last coin while the queen is not covered, gives the board to the opponent with the published points, and a tie after board 8 plays a ninth `Extra board`.

Create a private room
A host who creates a Quick room through `button "Create a room"` reaches `/room/<code>` with a 6-character code from the published alphabet, the full join link, `Waiting for opponent...`, and `#room-expiry` counting down from the server's remaining time whatever the device clock says.

Join by link, ready and toss
A second player who opens the link joins with `button "Join"`, both names appear on both pages, both press `button "Ready"` (one by keyboard), the toss line names the host when `TOSS_SEED` is 0, and both reach the same `/match/<id>` with the host to break.

Room full for a third player
A third player who opens the link sees `heading "Room full"` and `This room already has two players.`

Join with a code by keyboard
On `/join` the six `textbox "Character <n> of 6"` boxes turn a typed lower-case code into upper case with focus moving on, Backspace in an empty box moves back, a pasted code fills all six, and Enter joins.

Rematch in the same room
After a private match ends, the host's `button "Rematch"` shows `<name> wants a rematch.` live and announced on the other page, and accepting by keyboard starts a new match in the same room at 0-0 with the breaker swapped.

One joiner and room expiry
When two joins arrive at the same moment, exactly one answers `200` and the other `409 ROOM_FULL`, and a room left without a joiner past `ROOM_EXPIRY_SECONDS` by server time answers `410 ROOM_CLOSED`.

Link an email for ranked
A guest who presses `button "Play ranked"` gets `dialog "Link your email"`, `button "Send link"` shows `Link sent to <email>. Open it on any device.` only after the mail server accepts the message, and opening the emailed link shows `Email linked: <email>` and lets Play ranked enter the queue.

Queue screen readouts
A linked player rated 1500 in the ranked queue sees `Looking for players near 1500` and `Rating band: 1400-1600`.

Band widens and pairs live
On the short-timer instance, linked players rated 1500 and 1700 see their band widen live to `1350-1650` and then `1300-1700`, and both reach the same `/match/<id>` as a `Ranked` match with the earlier joiner in seat 0.

Cancel the queue by Escape
Escape on the queue screen cancels the same way `button "Cancel"` does, returns to `/`, and that player is no longer paired.

Queue radar motion and reduced motion
`#radar` sweeps once every 1.6 seconds while waiting and does not turn with reduced motion.

Pairing once and the ranked lock
Three players entering one queue at the same moment produce exactly one pair and one waiting player, and a guest without a linked email gets `403 LINK_REQUIRED`.

Server shot clock passes the turn
On the short-timer instance `#shot-timer` starts at `0:04`, and if no shot is made the server passes the turn with `TIME UP` and `Time's up. The turn passes.` on both pages and no due.

Three timeouts forfeit
A player's third consecutive timeout ends the match, and the opponent sees `You won` and `<name> forfeited: 3 timeouts in a row`.

Reconnecting overlay
When one player goes offline, the other sees `#reconnect-overlay` with `<name> is reconnecting... <m:ss>` announced once, and the offline page shows `Connection lost. Reconnecting...`.

Rejoin within the window
A player who comes back online and reloads within the reconnect window gets their seat back with identical pieces and scores, and the overlay goes away.

Ranked forfeit after the window
When a ranked player stays away past the window, the opponent sees `You won`, `<name> forfeited: left the match` and `Rating 1662 (+162)` for two new players, and both players' histories show the rating change after reload.

Buy and keep a striker skin
With 300 chalk, buying Cobalt Ring leaves `50 chalk` and shows `button "Equip Cobalt Ring"`, both are still there after reload, and the ledger sum equals the balance.

Shop by keyboard
Arrow keys move between the three tabs of `tablist "Item kinds"` with roving focus and `aria-selected`, and Enter buys an item and then equips it.

Short balance disables Buy
With 130 chalk `button "Buy Cobalt Ring"` is disabled and reads `Need 120 more`.

Double tap debits once
Two quick taps on `button "Buy Cobalt Ring"` debit 250 chalk only once, leaving one purchase movement in the ledger and a balance of 50.

Equipped skin seen by the opponent
After the buyer equips Cobalt Ring and Walnut Night, the opponent's page shows `piece-striker` with `data-skin="striker-cobalt"` on the buyer's turn, while `#board` with `data-theme="board-walnut"` shows only on the buyer's page.

Purchase rules and paired ledger
A short balance answers `402 INSUFFICIENT_CHALK` with `needed`, a repeated `idempotencyKey` debits only once, and every chalk movement is two ledger entries that sum to zero.

Run manifest and health
`/app/run.json` installs, builds and serves the app on port 4173, and `GET /api/health` always answers 200 with `{"status":"ok"}` or `{"status":"unavailable"}`.

Server boundary
The server refuses cross-origin writes and socket upgrades, oversized bodies and non-JSON bodies with the published errors, never serves source, configuration or credentials, and the browser never requests another origin.

Database outage
With PostgreSQL unreachable every page loads with the database outage banner, online buttons are disabled, and a resigned pass-and-play match ends with `Saved on this device. It will be added to your history when online.`

Mail outage
With mail unreachable, Send link answers `503 MAIL_UNAVAILABLE` and shows `We couldn't send the link. Try again in a minute.`, the player stays unlinked, and ranked stays locked while guest play works.

Magic link sign-in on another device
Opening a sign-in link for an email that already belongs to another player signs this browser in as that player with `Signed in as <name>`, and a used or expired link shows `heading "This link has expired"`.

Verdict swap field wipe
When the turn passes, `#field-wipe` crosses the viewport from the incoming player's baseline edge in about 520 ms, and `#match-root` `data-turn` and `data-field` change only at its end, or at once with reduced motion.

Published breakpoints
At 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 the match screen arranges the board and score rail as published, the whole board stays in view while aiming, nothing scrolls sideways, and every control is at least 44 px.

Accessibility and visible focus
Home, match, shop and profile have no automated accessibility violations at the three published sizes, and every focused control shows a visible focus ring.

Shared deterministic model
`POST /api/grading/simulate` reproduces the published physics set-ups, and the same input always returns byte-identical events and final positions.

Glicko-2 ratings, tiers and leaderboard
Each ranked match is one Glicko-2 rating period with the published constants and worked examples, tiers follow the published bands, and the leaderboard lists only eligible players plus the viewer's own row.

Chalk awards
Completed online matches, first daily wins and pass-and-play matches award the published chalk exactly once per player, and forfeits and abandoned matches award none as qualified in Business rules.

Preset emotes
`button "Emotes"` offers six preset emotes, a sent emote appears and is announced on the opponent's page, and an unknown emote answers `422 INVALID_EMOTE`.

Grading routes
The grading routes create players, matches and ruled events exactly as published when `X-Grading-Key` matches `GRADING_KEY`, and answer 404 otherwise.

Duotone turn fields
Each match screen is one saturated field in the current shooter's colour, tomato with ink type for seat 0 and cobalt with white type for seat 1, with the square board centred and the opponent's name cropped huge behind it.

Procedural board and pieces
The board is a drawn object of lacquered ply with four net pockets, baselines and centre circle, and its coins, queen and striker skins are all drawn by the app without image files.

Working screens in the same language
History, profile, shop, room lobby, empty states and outage banners use the same Chivo type, square-cornered surfaces, giant cropped words and two-colour fields as the match screen.

One rules module in source
One shared, pure module holds the physics step and the laws of carrom, and both the browser and the server import it with no copy of either rule set elsewhere.

Configuration from the environment
Every service address, credential, timer and grading key is read from the environment at start, is never hard-coded, and never reaches the browser.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package with its licence, plus the Chivo font and Lucide icons; shipped packages means the production dependency tree (npm ls --omit=dev --all --json).
Every shipped package and asset is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or SIL OFL 1.1.
PostgreSQL is the only datastore; no other database, cache, queue, object store or realtime service is added, and the app writes no data files on the server.
All server and client source is TypeScript.
The provided service configuration (the development compose fragments for PostgreSQL and Mailpit) is left unchanged.
/app contains no virtual environment and no absolute symlinks.
